facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base supports a bounded reported-fact view of Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. at the consolidated level, with specific limits. Reported FY2024 and FY2025 statements are audited and consolidated. Six-month 2026 and 2025 statements are unaudited. The base is dominated by the January 2026 acquisitions of CAC Group, Obie and Capstone, which closed against a 600,000 thousand incremental term loan, new equity and new contingent claims. As a result the 2025 comparatives and the FY2025 balance sheet are not like for like with 2026. On the company's adjusted EBITDA definition, total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.59x at FY2024, 5.01x at FY2025 and 6.30x on a last-twelve-months basis to 2026-06-30, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x. Cash interest cover on the same earnings is 2.81x, 2.96x and 2.89x. These ratios are calculated here from printed components and are not company-reported credit metrics. Three limits bind every use. First, adjusted EBITDA carries large management addbacks, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, is far lower, so the leverage view depends on which earnings measure a reader accepts. Second, the last-twelve-months earnings include six months of acquired earnings while the 2026-06-30 debt carries the full acquisition financing, and a pro forma adjusted EBITDA for the 2026 acquisitions is not supplied, so the 6.30x is probably overstated relative to a full-year acquired run rate by an amount the pack does not size. Third, the single financial maintenance covenant, a total first lien net leverage test, is described only in the 10-K, with no reported ratio, so headroom is not calculable. Liquidity is stated by the company at the latest date. Debt maturities after the January 2026 add-on are derived here, not printed. No perimeter other than the consolidated group is supplied.

Cash interest cover on the same earnings is 2.81x, 2.96x and 2.89x. These ratios are calculated here from printed components and are not company-reported credit metrics. Three limits bind every use. First, adjusted EBITDA carries large management addbacks, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, is far lower, so the leverage view depends on which earnings measure a reader accepts. Second, the last-twelve-months earnings include six months of acquired earnings while the 2026-06-30 debt carries the full acquisition financing, and a pro forma adjusted EBITDA for the 2026 acquisitions is not supplied, so the 6.30x is probably overstated relative to a full-year acquired run rate by an amount the pack does not size. Third, the single financial maintenance covenant, a total first lien net leverage test, is described only in the 10-K, with no reported ratio, so headroom is not calculable. Liquidity is stated by the company at the latest date. Debt maturities after the January 2026 add-on are derived here, not printed. No perimeter other than the consolidated group is supplied.

facts.label: Narrative findings
facts.text: - Leverage and the earnings measure. Evidence: calculated total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 against 5.01x at FY2025, and adjustments other than interest, amortization and depreciation were 48.6% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA. Risk mechanism: the acquisition debt is fully in the numerator while only six months of acquired earnings is in the denominator, and management addbacks are a large share of the earnings, so the ratio can move materially with the covenant definition. Creditor implication: the first lien covenant at 7.00x (10-K page:164) cannot be tested from the pack, and the adjusted figure should not be read as covenant headroom. - Interest burden. Evidence: net interest expense of 144,698 for the last twelve months and cash interest cover of 2.89x. Risk mechanism: the Term Loans and revolver are floating, with a 500,000 swap to a fixed 3.244% covering part of the exposure, and the notes at 7.125% pay semi-annually, so quarterly cover is seasonal (2.10x in Q2 2025 and 2.33x in Q2 2026, both quarters containing the May coupon). Creditor implication: the six-month trend in cover fell from 3.66x to 3.33x as interest rose faster than adjusted earnings; the 100 bp sensitivity is 14.0 million a year. - Liquidity. Evidence: cash of 184.5 million and undrawn capacity of 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against 123.7 million and 477.0 million at 2025-12-31. Risk mechanism: revolver drawings rose by a net 195,000 in six months while cash paid for repurchases and acquisition-related payments was large. Creditor implication: liquidity remains sizeable against near-term scheduled debt service, but the buffer fell and sits ahead of a 2029 revolver maturity and 346,824 of earnout liabilities. - Claims outside debt. Evidence: earnouts of 346,824, deferred payments of 192,500 undiscounted and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of 144,570. Risk mechanism: these are contractual or probable cash outflows that compete with debt service, and the earnouts are at fair value with a maximum for the 2026 deals of 544,855. Creditor implication: debt-only leverage understates fixed and contingent cash claims; downstream work must show them separately. - Cash conversion. Evidence: net cash from operations of 39,486 for six months 2026 and an outflow of 80,704 for six months 2025, with earnout payments in excess of the accrual of 6,739 and 85,090. Risk mechanism: most of the swing is lower earnout payments and no colleague earnout incentive payments inside operating cash flow (31,824 in 6M 2025), so cash flow before earnouts is a better indicator of conversion. Creditor implication: adjusted free cash flow of 46,225 is the company's definition and adds back earnout payments; it should not be mistaken for free cash flow after all acquisition-related payments. - Comparability. Evidence: acquired businesses added revenue of 202.1 million in six months 2026 while organic revenue growth was 2% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:17, page:60). Risk mechanism: the reported 29% revenue growth for six months mostly reflects acquisitions. Creditor implication: use organic and pro forma measures to judge underlying trend.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. is a publicly listed holding company whose sole material asset is its interest in The Baldwin Insurance Group Holdings, LLC, the operating company, borrower and note issuer. It distributes commercial property and casualty, employee benefits, personal lines, wealth and retirement, and Medicare products through three operating groups, and manufactures proprietary insurance products through its managing general agent platform. The credit story of the period is a step change in scale and leverage. Three partnerships, led by CAC Group, closed on 2026-01-01 and 2026-01-02 for total consideration of 1,559,612 thousand, financed through a mix of 600,000 thousand of incremental term loans under Amendment No. 4, Class A shares issued to sellers, contingent earnouts and deferred payments, while cash and revolver borrowing also rose over the period. No private-equity sponsor owns the issuer. Control rights instead rest with the pre-IPO members of the operating company, who hold Class B shares and, under a stockholders agreement that the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated on 2026-06-09, approval rights over mergers, large asset deals, borrowing above stated thresholds, equity issuance and dividends. Revenue is recurring in form, since it is commissions, fees and carrier bonuses on renewing policies, but it follows premium levels and carrier relationships, and the reported growth for the first half of 2026 is mostly acquired. The facts that matter most to a creditor are the acquisition-related cash claims outside debt, the insider approval rights and the absence of a supplied credit agreement, so permitted debt, restricted payments and guarantor perimeter cannot be tested here. The view is Medium confidence: the business and transaction facts are well documented, while ownership percentages, governance practice and legal capacity are not.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: CAC Group (Cobbs Allen Capital Holdings, LLC) was acquired effective 2026-01-01 under a Transaction Agreement dated 2025-12-02 (exhibit 10.32 in the 10-K exhibit list, page:200), amended 2025-12-30. The 10-K describes closing consideration of 438.0 million of cash, 23,200,000 Class A shares and a deferred payment of 70.0 million payable on the fourth anniversary, with contingent consideration payable in cash on post-closing revenue targets (10-K page:188). Obie (Creisoft, Inc.) and Capstone (Foley Insurance Agency, Inc.) were acquired effective 2026-01-02. Obie's consideration was stated as 90.0 million of cash and 396,573 shares plus 122.5 million of deferred payments (10-K page:188). In aggregate the three businesses were recorded at total consideration of 1,559,612 thousand, comprising cash of 567,889, contingent earnouts at fair value of 315,998, equity of 510,561 and deferred payments of 165,164, with goodwill of 1,134,895 and intangible assets of 550,983, and a maximum potential contingent earnout of 544,855 (page:16-19). The purchase accounting is provisional. These businesses contributed total revenues of 202.1 million and a net loss of 42.3 million in six months 2026 (page:17). Management says CAC Group integration is "meaningfully ahead of plan, with approximately 80% of targeted three-year expense synergies already actioned" (Q1 release page:1); that is Management Language and the pack gives no synergy bridge.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: commissions follow premium levels and carrier profit-sharing varies, with organic growth of 2% for six months 2026 (10-K page:8; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:60). Mechanic: a soft market lowers premium-based commissions while the people cost base is largely fixed. Implication: margin and debt service capacity are exposed to the premium cycle, and acquired growth does not show underlying durability. The two carriers providing approximately 17% of core commissions and fees counter the diversification across clients. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: the 10-Q shows Tax Receivable Agreement expense of 128.8 million, contingent consideration fair value changes of 14,272 and large addbacks in adjusted EBITDA (financial base). Mechanic: acquisition-related items run through earnings and cash, and earnout payments sit in operating cash flow. Implication: free cash flow after earnouts is lower than the company's adjusted free cash flow, and conversion depends on payment timing. - Concentration risk. Evidence: two carriers at approximately 17% of core commissions and fees, a Southeastern history and several regional concentrations (10-K page:14, page:24). Mechanic: a loss of carrier appetite or a regional catastrophe hits revenue and profit-sharing together. Implication: a downside case should stress carrier and regional exposure, not client count. - Sponsor alignment and control. Evidence: no sponsor; holders' approval rights over debt, dividends and bankruptcy filing back in force (10-Q Q2 2026 page:39; 10-K page:73). Mechanic: control sits with insiders who are also Tax Receivable Agreement creditors and Class B holders. Implication: creditors face insider-controlled leverage decisions without an independent committee check, while no extraction is documented. The logged conflict on Tax Receivable Agreement history is the one counter-point to a clean disclosure read. - Key uncertainties. Purchase accounting is provisional, the earnout maximum is 544,855, covenant compliance after 2025-12-31 is not stated, and later-period events to 2026-11-05 are not supplied.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. has an elevated-leverage but adequately liquid credit profile, and this synthesis holds that view with Medium confidence. Its strongest support is a diversified, commission-based client base, first-lien debt with no maturity before the revolver on 2029-05-24 beyond scheduled amortization, and USD 184.5 million of cash plus USD 259.4 million of undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-06-30. The weakest point is leverage: total debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 from 5.01x at FY2025, on earnings that rely on large addbacks and hold only six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. Whether acquired earnings reach run rate, whether earnout and deferred payments are met without new borrowing, and covenant headroom, which is not supplied, decide the outcome.

The weakest point is leverage: total debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 from 5.01x at FY2025, on earnings that rely on large addbacks and hold only six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. Whether acquired earnings reach run rate, whether earnout and deferred payments are met without new borrowing, and covenant headroom, which is not supplied, decide the outcome.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage rose in each period. Baldwin's total debt, including the revolver, was USD 1,435.8 million at FY2024, USD 1,710.6 million at FY2025 and USD 2,495.0 million at 2026-06-30, giving total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.59x, 5.01x and 6.30x, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x [financial base, leverage chart]. The mechanism is the USD 600.0 million incremental term loan of 2026-01-02 and revolver drawings that rose by USD 195.0 million in six months, set against adjusted EBITDA of USD 396.2 million for the last twelve months that includes about six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. The implication is that the 6.30x probably overstates leverage relative to a full-year pro forma basis by an amount the sources do not size, while the use of company-defined earnings could push the other way, so the ratio is an indicator and not a covenant test.

facts.text: Second, earnings quality limits every ratio. Adjustments other than interest, amortization and depreciation were 42.5% of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and 48.6% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, was USD 58.1 million for the last twelve months against USD 396.2 million adjusted [financial base]. The gap includes USD 128.8 million of Tax Receivable Agreement expense recognized in six months 2026, which the company adds back although the liability is a future cash obligation. The implication is that creditors who underwrite on adjusted EBITDA are relying on management's definition, and the covenant EBITDA may differ.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, interest cover held while leverage rose. Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest was 2.81x at FY2024, 2.96x at FY2025 and 2.89x for the last twelve months, but the six-month figure fell from 3.66x to 3.33x as cash interest rose faster than adjusted earnings [financial base]. About USD 500.0 million of the floating-rate term loans is swapped to a fixed 3.244% to 2028-09-14, and a 100 bp rise in SOFR would add USD 14.0 million a year to interest. The implication is that cover is moderate relative to leverage but protected for part of the rate exposure until 2028.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, liquidity is adequate and narrowing. Cash and equivalents were USD 184.5 million and company-stated undrawn revolver capacity USD 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against USD 123.7 million and USD 477.0 million at FY2025, with USD 302.0 million drawn on a USD 600.0 million revolver [financial base, liquidity chart]. The implication is that near-term liquidity covers scheduled amortization of about USD 16.0 million a year, derived, but it is more exposed to cash calls from earnouts and the Tax Receivable Agreement.

Contingent earnout liabilities were USD 346.8 million at fair value, with undiscounted expected payments of USD 410.5 million of which USD 131.1 million fall within one year, deferred payments were USD 192.5 million undiscounted, and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities were USD 144.6 million at 2026-06-30 [financial base]. The January 2026 acquisitions cost USD 1,559.6 million in total, of which equity was USD 510.6 million and the maximum potential earnout is USD 544.9 million [business and transaction]. The implication is that the true fixed-claim burden exceeds the debt total, and a strong year for the acquired businesses raises earnout payments in cash.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Sixth, control and governance have changed. The Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Court of Chancery on 2026-06-09, the 2024 Stockholders Agreement is in effect, and holders have stated approval rights over debt above 10% of total assets, dividends, large asset transactions and a bankruptcy filing, while the independent committee created in 2024 has been disbanded [business and transaction]. There is no sponsor, and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented. The implication is that leverage and distribution decisions are insider-influenced, and how approvals were applied to the 2025 and 2026 debt additions is not disclosed, so legal capacity cannot be assessed.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Seventh, the business is diversified by client but not by carrier or cycle. The largest client is under 1% of core commissions and fees, while two insurance partners provided about 17%; commissions follow premium levels, organic revenue growth was 2% for six months 2026 against reported growth of 29%, and the Captive adds underwriting exposure of USD 29.5 million of assumed premium earned in six months 2026 [business and transaction]. The implication is that revenue is durable against any single client but exposed to a soft premium market and carrier appetite, and the growth in the period was bought rather than organic.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Baldwin's client base is highly diversified, with more than three million clients and no client above 1% of core commissions and fees, so single-client loss is not a credit driver [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Its funded debt is long-dated, with the revolver due 2029-05-24 and the term loans and the 7.125% senior secured notes due in 2031, so refinancing risk is back-ended beyond scheduled amortization [financial base; Analyst Interpretation, because the maturity rows are derived]. Liquidity of USD 184.5 million of cash and USD 259.4 million of undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-06-30 covers near-term scheduled amortization many times over [financial base; Documentary Fact for the inputs]. Cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA has stayed near 2.9x across three periods, and part of the floating-rate exposure is fixed by a USD 500.0 million swap at 3.244% to 2028-09-14 [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditures of USD 39.5 million in FY2025, so cash flow is driven by earnouts, interest and acquisitions rather than reinvestment [financial base; Analyst Interpretation]. Management reports faster integration of CAC Group than planned, but this is Management Language and carries no supporting bridge [business and transaction; Management Language].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.30x for the last twelve months and net debt to adjusted EBITDA 5.83x, up from 5.01x and 4.65x at FY2025, with the denominator holding only about six months of acquired earnings [financial base; Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on addbacks of 48.6% over interest, amortization and depreciation, and the reported result is a net loss of USD 131.8 million for the last twelve months [financial base; Documentary Fact]. All funded debt ranks as first lien and is secured on substantially all assets, so the structure has no subordinated layer beneath the term loans, revolver and notes [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Claims outside debt are material: earnouts of USD 346.8 million, deferred payments of USD 192.5 million and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of USD 144.6 million [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Operating cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 43.7 million for the last twelve months and negative USD 68.9 million in FY2025, because earnout payments in excess of the accrual run through operations [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Revenue growth is mostly acquired, with organic growth of 2% for six months 2026 [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Control rests with insiders through approval rights over debt, dividends and a bankruptcy filing, with the independent committee disbanded, and Tax Receivable Agreement payments are owed to LLC members [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Two insurance partners provided about 17% of core commissions and fees, and the book was historically concentrated in the Southeast [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. The financial maintenance covenant of 7.00x total first lien net leverage is described only in the FY2025 annual report, with no later reported ratio, so headroom is unmeasured [financial base; Insufficient Information].

Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This module gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion. It does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Arithmetic in `## Calculations` is limited to tie-outs that test source consistency and to coverage counts.

The context file holds the run settings and is not issuer evidence. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases through the second quarter of 2026 are enough to build the financial base, debt picture and business context, with bounded limits. | Medium | The credit agreement, indenture and covenant compliance figures are not supplied, and the large January 2026 acquisitions change comparability. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The financial maintenance covenant is described only in the annual report, and no later report states a ratio or compliance. | Covenant headroom cannot be measured from the pack; only the company's stated borrowing capacity is available. | High |
| Debt terms, balances and the January 2026 term loan add-on are printed in the latest quarterly report. | Facility sizes, balances, rates and maturities can be set out from the filing. | High |

| Three acquisitions closed in January 2026, alongside higher revenue, debt, earnout and deferred payment balances, against prior-year comparatives that exclude them. | Year-over-year figures mix acquired and organic results, so downstream work must use the stated organic and pro forma measures. | High |

| Segment profit is disclosed as net income only; segment adjusted EBITDA, ratings and guarantor names are not supplied. | Segment cash earnings, rating context and the guarantor perimeter are open gaps. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations. All four requested consumers are assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS; none is CONDITIONAL and none is BLOCKED. The audited annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases cover the periods the context names, in the reporting currency, with the latest dated 2026-07-30, before the 2026-11-05 cutoff. The binding limitations are five. First, no executed legal document is supplied, so covenant levels, guarantor lists and security terms rest on filing summaries, and the quarterly reports print no covenant compliance statement at all. Second, the January 2026 acquisitions of CAC Group, Obie and Capstone make the 2025 comparatives and the FY2025 base differ in perimeter from the 2026 reports. Third, segment adjusted EBITDA is not disclosed in the segment note. Fourth, no fidelity review of the text extraction was done, and the pack contains no slides or charts. Fifth, no report for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 is supplied, so the latest balance sheet is 2026-06-30. None of these blocks a consumer from starting, and each carries forward as a stated limit.
### Source-by-source assessment

All seven sources identify The Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. as registrant or announcing company (page:1 of each). No source is blocked, draft, unsigned or a duplicate of another; the three releases and the quarterly reports overlap in content but are different documents. The filed 10-K and 10-Qs control their own facts. The releases are management claims and must not override a filing.
| Source | What it supports | Limit |

| 10-K FY2025 | Audited statements (auditor report page:128; balance sheet page:131-132; income statement page:132; cash flows page:134-135), debt note 12 (page:161-165), covenant text (page:164), debt maturities (page:165), segment note (page:183-186), subsequent events including the January 2026 acquisitions and Amendment No. 4 (page:188-189), Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (page:99), exhibit list (page:196-200) | The exhibit list names the indenture and credit agreement amendments but does not reproduce them; maturities are as of 2025-12-31, before the January 2026 add-on |

| 10-Q Q3 2025 | Nine-month 2025 statements (page:5-6, page:9), debt note (page:28), segments (page:38), Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (page:55), liquidity (page:68) | Supplies the third-quarter 2025 discrete period and 2024 comparatives |
| 10-Q Q1 2026 | Q1 2026 statements (page:5-8), debt note including Amendment No. 4 (page:23), segments (page:39), Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (page:54), liquidity (page:65) | Unaudited |

| 10-Q Q2 2026 | Statements (balance sheet page:5-6, income page:6-7, cash flows page:9-10), business combinations (page:16-19), debt (page:24-25), fair value of debt (page:38), segments (page:40-44), subsequent events (page:46-47), non-GAAP reconciliations (page:58-61), liquidity and contractual obligations (page:72-75), controls (page:82-83) | Unaudited; no covenant text; no principal maturity table |
| EX-99.1 2026-02-26 | Q4 and FY2025 headline results, share repurchase authorization, adjusted free cash flow definition change (page:1, page:12) | Management claims |
| EX-99.1 2026-05-04 | Q1 2026 headlines and adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (page:1, page:11) | Management claims |

| EX-99.1 2026-07-30 | Q2 2026 headlines, liquidity sentence, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow reconciliations (page:1-2, page:11, page:13) | Management claims; guidance has no GAAP reconciliation (page:11) |
### Entity and perimeter

The registrant is The Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc., a holding company whose "sole material asset is its ownership interest in Baldwin Holdings" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:11). The operating company and borrower is The Baldwin Insurance Group Holdings, LLC ("Baldwin Holdings"), defined at 10-Q Q2 2026 page:4 and named "as borrower" under the JPM Credit Agreement (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4). The statements are consolidated with Baldwin Holdings and carry a noncontrolling interest for LLC Units held by others (page:11). No stand-alone financial statements of Baldwin Holdings or of the issuer group are supplied, so debt-level analysis rests on consolidated figures. This is a perimeter gap, not a conclusion.

The 7.125% Senior Secured Notes were issued by Baldwin Holdings and a wholly-owned corporate subsidiary of Baldwin Holdings, called the co-issuer (10-K page:161); the exhibit list names the co-issuer as The Baldwin Insurance Group Holdings Finance, Inc. (10-K page:196). The notes and the JPM Credit Facility are guaranteed by certain direct and indirect subsidiaries of Baldwin Holdings (10-K page:163); no guarantor is named in the pack. Exhibit 21.1, the list of subsidiaries, is marked as filed with the 10-K (page:200) but its text is not in the pack. Security is "substantially all the assets of Baldwin Holdings and the guarantors" (10-K page:163). The Tax Receivable Agreement is an obligation of the parent, not of Baldwin Holdings (10-Q Q2 2026 page:15). Consolidated variable interest entities have assets usable only to settle their own obligations and creditors of those entities have no recourse to the Company (10-Q Q2 2026 page:6, page:20).
### Period basis and version relationships

Statements are unaudited for the interim periods and audited for FY2025. The balance sheet at 2025-12-31 in the interim reports is derived from the audited statements (10-Q Q2 2026 page:12). The interim income statements use three-month and six-month columns (Q2 2026 page:6-7); the Q3 2025 report uses three-month and nine-month columns. A discrete Q4 2025 therefore comes from the Q4 release (page:1, page:5) or from the FY2025 less nine-month 2025 figures, which is downstream work and is not done here. Discrete Q1 2026 is in the Q1 10-Q, and discrete Q2 2026 in the Q2 10-Q.

The perimeter changes inside the pack. Three business combinations with aggregate purchase price of $1.6 billion closed in the first half of 2026: CAC Group effective 2026-01-01, Obie and Capstone effective 2026-01-02 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:16-17; 10-K page:188-189). The 10-K and Q3 2025 report precede them; the 10-K describes them as subsequent events and says the company had not yet completed its evaluation of the identifiable assets and liabilities acquired (10-K page:188). The Q2 10-Q still describes purchase price allocations as provisional (page:18). The Q2 10-Q provides pro forma results as if the acquisitions had occurred on 2025-01-01 (page:19-20) and organic revenue growth (page:60). Reported 2025 comparatives and the FY2025 base do not include the acquired businesses; pro forma and organic figures are the only like-for-like bridges supplied.

The 10-K debt note mixes periods. Its narrative still describes the 2024 Term Loans at a margin of 325 bps and revolver margins of 200 bps to 300 bps (10-K page:162) before later paragraphs reprice them to 250 bps and 175 bps to 250 bps (10-K page:164-165). The later paragraphs supersede the earlier text. The Q2 10-Q gives the revolver margin as "SOFR plus 185 bps to SOFR plus 260 bps" in the liquidity section (page:73) and as a 10 bps credit spread adjustment plus 175 bps to 250 bps in Note 10 (page:24). These are the same range once the adjustment is added; see Calculations.

Interest expense differs between the income statement and the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliations. The Q2 10-Q footnote says "Interest expense, net does not include interest income on surplus notes" (page:61). The Q2 reconciliation uses 46,140 for the quarter against 45,666 on the income statement (release page:11; 10-Q page:7), and the 10-K reconciliation uses 122,778 against 121,428 (page:99; page:132). This is a labelled definition difference, not an error. Downstream work must say which one it uses.

Version relationship among documents: Amendment Nos. 1 to 4 to the JPM Credit Agreement are separate active amendments to the base agreement dated 2024-05-24 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4). The 10-K exhibit list names the base agreement and each amendment (exhibits 10.27 to 10.31, page:199-200), the indenture (exhibit 4.1, page:196) and the CAC Group Transaction Agreement dated 2025-12-02 with its amendment (exhibits 10.32 and 10.33, page:200). None of these documents is supplied; they remain separate sources to obtain, not collapsed into the filings that summarize them.
### Debt and liquidity evidence present

The Q2 10-Q gives, at 2026-06-30: Term Loans of "$1.6 billion" at 6.13% maturing 2031-05-24; Revolving Facility commitments of $600 million maturing 2029-05-24 with $302.0 million drawn at 6.23%; 7.125% Senior Secured Notes of $600 million due 2031-05-15; undrawn letters of credit under the revolver of $38.6 million; a commitment fee of 0.40% on unused capacity; quarterly Term Loan principal payments of $4.0 million (page:24-25, page:73). The exact principal is in the fair-value table: long-term debt carrying amount 2,193,045 thousand and revolver 302,000 thousand (page:38). The same table's footnote says unamortized discount and issuance costs are $26.2 million, and the balance sheet shows revolving line of credit 302,000, long-term debt less current portion 2,150,725 and a current portion of long-term debt of 16,091 within accrued expenses (page:5, page:23). A $500 million floating-to-fixed swap at 3.244% runs to 2028-09-14 (page:25). The company states cash and cash equivalents of $184.5 million and $259.4 million of available borrowing capacity on the revolver (page:74; release page:2). Fiduciary cash of 426,189 thousand is shown separately from cash and cash equivalents of 184,499 thousand on the balance sheet (page:5) and is not unrestricted cash.

Claims outside the debt figure that are printed: contingent earnout liabilities of 120,901 thousand current and 225,923 thousand non-current; Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of 144,570 thousand; other liabilities of 129,376 thousand, which include the non-current deferred payment obligations of $129.4 million (page:5, page:19); operating lease liabilities (page:5, page:74-75); and a University of South Florida commitment of $2.5 million through October 2028 (page:38). The contractual obligations table at page:74 gives totals by period for operating leases, debt obligations including estimated interest, undiscounted earnout obligations, deferred payments and the USF grant. The company has a $250 million share repurchase authorization announced 2026-02-26, with approximately $124.5 million remaining at 2026-06-30 (page:83).

The 10-K reports at 2025-12-31: cash and cash equivalents 123,669 thousand, $477.0 million of available revolver capacity (page:110), principal amount of long-term debt 1,603,606 thousand with maturities by year (page:165) and cash paid for interest 115,276 thousand and cash paid for taxes 1,700 thousand for FY2025 (page:135). The Q2 10-Q gives cash paid for interest of 76,315 thousand and for income taxes of 759 thousand for six months 2026 (page:10).

The pack does not give: a principal maturity table at 2026-06-30 after the January 2026 add-on (the 10-K table is as of 2025-12-31; the Q2 contractual obligations table includes interest); an amortization-adjusted exact term loan balance (only "$1.6 billion" and the implied figure derived in Calculations); fair value of the term loans separately from the notes; or any pension or retiree medical obligation beyond a 401(k) plan with employer matching (10-K page:16, page:127 index "Retirement Plan"). Factoring and supply-chain finance did not appear in a search of all seven sources.
### Covenants

The only financial maintenance test printed is in the 10-K: "a financial maintenance covenant requiring Baldwin Holdings to maintain a total first lien net leverage ratio at or below 7.00 to 1.00 on a pro forma basis", with compliance stated at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:164). The Senior Secured Notes indenture limits the issuers and restricted subsidiaries on debt, liens, restricted payments, affiliate transactions and mergers, with compliance stated at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:162). The 10-K also gives the incremental facility test of 5.50x total first lien net leverage and a margin step-down at 4.00x first lien net leverage (10-K page:162-163). A search of all seven sources for covenant, 7.00, financial maintenance, springing, fixed charge and interest coverage found covenant wording only in the 10-K. The Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 reports contain none, and no source prints the reported first lien net leverage ratio, the definition of consolidated EBITDA or whether the test applies at all times or only when the revolver is drawn. Covenant headroom is therefore not calculable from the pack. The 7.00x test is "on a pro forma basis" and its defined terms are not supplied, so they may differ from the company's adjusted EBITDA and from GAAP debt; downstream work must not equate them.

Evidence present for 2026 up to the filing of the Q2 10-Q: the three acquisitions and their consideration (CAC Group 1,220,213 thousand, Obie 287,370 thousand, Capstone 52,029 thousand; page:18); Amendment No. 4 with $600 million of incremental term loans on 2026-01-02 and about $12.0 million of debt issuance costs (page:25); a loss on extinguishment and modification of debt of 7,538 thousand for six months (page:7); recognition of Tax Receivable Agreement expense of $128.8 million (page:72) and an income tax benefit of 144,437 thousand for six months from a partial valuation allowance release (page:7, page:29-30); a held-for-sale plan for Media Guarantors, with a definitive sale agreement dated 2026-07-02 for $4.0 million of cash (page:46-47); and share repurchases of 3,839,937 shares in Q2 under the program (page:83). Disclosure controls were concluded effective at 2026-06-30 with no change in internal control (page:82-83); the FY2025 auditor's report states that the statements present fairly and that internal control over financial reporting was maintained effectively in all material respects (10-K page:128). Legal proceedings are stated as ordinary course with no material adverse effect expected (page:38). Item 3 of Part II, defaults upon senior securities, states "None" (page:83). Nothing in the pack is dated after 2026-07-30. No fact dated after 2026-11-05 is relied on.

The pack has no report for the quarter ended 2026-09-30. The context names Q2 2026 as the current period, so this is consistent with the request. Whether a later report exists at the as-of date is not known from the sources, and events between 2026-07-30 and 2026-11-05 are Not supplied, not absent.

### Financial base view

The financial base supports a bounded reported-fact view of Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. at the consolidated level, with specific limits. Reported FY2024 and FY2025 statements are audited and consolidated. Six-month 2026 and 2025 statements are unaudited. The base is dominated by the January 2026 acquisitions of CAC Group, Obie and Capstone, which closed against a 600,000 thousand incremental term loan, new equity and new contingent claims. As a result the 2025 comparatives and the FY2025 balance sheet are not like for like with 2026. On the company's adjusted EBITDA definition, total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.59x at FY2024, 5.01x at FY2025 and 6.30x on a last-twelve-months basis to 2026-06-30, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x. Cash interest cover on the same earnings is 2.81x, 2.96x and 2.89x. These ratios are calculated here from printed components and are not company-reported credit metrics. Three limits bind every use. First, adjusted EBITDA carries large management addbacks, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, is far lower, so the leverage view depends on which earnings measure a reader accepts. Second, the last-twelve-months earnings include six months of acquired earnings while the 2026-06-30 debt carries the full acquisition financing, and a pro forma adjusted EBITDA for the 2026 acquisitions is not supplied, so the 6.30x is probably overstated relative to a full-year acquired run rate by an amount the pack does not size. Third, the single financial maintenance covenant, a total first lien net leverage test, is described only in the 10-K, with no reported ratio, so headroom is not calculable. Liquidity is stated by the company at the latest date. Debt maturities after the January 2026 add-on are derived here, not printed. No perimeter other than the consolidated group is supplied.

### Narrative findings
Each finding runs from evidence to risk mechanism to creditor implication.

- Leverage and the earnings measure. Evidence: calculated total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 against 5.01x at FY2025, and adjustments other than interest, amortization and depreciation were 48.6% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA. Risk mechanism: the acquisition debt is fully in the numerator while only six months of acquired earnings is in the denominator, and management addbacks are a large share of the earnings, so the ratio can move materially with the covenant definition. Creditor implication: the first lien covenant at 7.00x (10-K page:164) cannot be tested from the pack, and the adjusted figure should not be read as covenant headroom.

- Interest burden. Evidence: net interest expense of 144,698 for the last twelve months and cash interest cover of 2.89x. Risk mechanism: the Term Loans and revolver are floating, with a 500,000 swap to a fixed 3.244% covering part of the exposure, and the notes at 7.125% pay semi-annually, so quarterly cover is seasonal (2.10x in Q2 2025 and 2.33x in Q2 2026, both quarters containing the May coupon). Creditor implication: the six-month trend in cover fell from 3.66x to 3.33x as interest rose faster than adjusted earnings; the 100 bp sensitivity is 14.0 million a year.

- Liquidity. Evidence: cash of 184.5 million and undrawn capacity of 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against 123.7 million and 477.0 million at 2025-12-31. Risk mechanism: revolver drawings rose by a net 195,000 in six months while cash paid for repurchases and acquisition-related payments was large. Creditor implication: liquidity remains sizeable against near-term scheduled debt service, but the buffer fell and sits ahead of a 2029 revolver maturity and 346,824 of earnout liabilities.

- Claims outside debt. Evidence: earnouts of 346,824, deferred payments of 192,500 undiscounted and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of 144,570. Risk mechanism: these are contractual or probable cash outflows that compete with debt service, and the earnouts are at fair value with a maximum for the 2026 deals of 544,855. Creditor implication: debt-only leverage understates fixed and contingent cash claims; downstream work must show them separately.

- Cash conversion. Evidence: net cash from operations of 39,486 for six months 2026 and an outflow of 80,704 for six months 2025, with earnout payments in excess of the accrual of 6,739 and 85,090. Risk mechanism: most of the swing is lower earnout payments and no colleague earnout incentive payments inside operating cash flow (31,824 in 6M 2025), so cash flow before earnouts is a better indicator of conversion. Creditor implication: adjusted free cash flow of 46,225 is the company's definition and adds back earnout payments; it should not be mistaken for free cash flow after all acquisition-related payments.

- Comparability. Evidence: acquired businesses added revenue of 202.1 million in six months 2026 while organic revenue growth was 2% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:17, page:60). Risk mechanism: the reported 29% revenue growth for six months mostly reflects acquisitions. Creditor implication: use organic and pro forma measures to judge underlying trend.

Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history and change. The view is creditor-side and limited to the supplied filings and releases. ### Reader summary

Creditor risks centre on insider approval rights over debt and dividends, acquisition-related cash claims, and premium-cycle and carrier concentration. | Medium | Ownership percentages, the credit agreement's permitted-debt capacity and how insider approval rights were applied are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Pre-IPO holders' approval rights, including over debt above 10% of total assets and over dividends, are back in force after the Delaware Supreme Court reversal on 2026-06-09. | Insiders can influence leverage and distributions; how approvals were applied to the current debt is not disclosed. | Medium |

### Business and transaction view

Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. is a publicly listed holding company whose sole material asset is its interest in The Baldwin Insurance Group Holdings, LLC, the operating company, borrower and note issuer. It distributes commercial property and casualty, employee benefits, personal lines, wealth and retirement, and Medicare products through three operating groups, and manufactures proprietary insurance products through its managing general agent platform. The credit story of the period is a step change in scale and leverage. Three partnerships, led by CAC Group, closed on 2026-01-01 and 2026-01-02 for total consideration of 1,559,612 thousand, financed through a mix of 600,000 thousand of incremental term loans under Amendment No. 4, Class A shares issued to sellers, contingent earnouts and deferred payments, while cash and revolver borrowing also rose over the period. No private-equity sponsor owns the issuer. Control rights instead rest with the pre-IPO members of the operating company, who hold Class B shares and, under a stockholders agreement that the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated on 2026-06-09, approval rights over mergers, large asset deals, borrowing above stated thresholds, equity issuance and dividends. Revenue is recurring in form, since it is commissions, fees and carrier bonuses on renewing policies, but it follows premium levels and carrier relationships, and the reported growth for the first half of 2026 is mostly acquired. The facts that matter most to a creditor are the acquisition-related cash claims outside debt, the insider approval rights and the absence of a supplied credit agreement, so permitted debt, restricted payments and guarantor perimeter cannot be tested here. The view is Medium confidence: the business and transaction facts are well documented, while ownership percentages, governance practice and legal capacity are not.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transactions in the pack are a set of completed acquisitions with debt financing, and there is no pending transaction at the cutoff other than a small disposal. Their status is completed unless stated. Source for the terms below is the Q2 2026 10-Q unless a different file is named.

CAC Group (Cobbs Allen Capital Holdings, LLC) was acquired effective 2026-01-01 under a Transaction Agreement dated 2025-12-02 (exhibit 10.32 in the 10-K exhibit list, page:200), amended 2025-12-30. The 10-K describes closing consideration of 438.0 million of cash, 23,200,000 Class A shares and a deferred payment of 70.0 million payable on the fourth anniversary, with contingent consideration payable in cash on post-closing revenue targets (10-K page:188). Obie (Creisoft, Inc.) and Capstone (Foley Insurance Agency, Inc.) were acquired effective 2026-01-02. Obie's consideration was stated as 90.0 million of cash and 396,573 shares plus 122.5 million of deferred payments (10-K page:188). In aggregate the three businesses were recorded at total consideration of 1,559,612 thousand, comprising cash of 567,889, contingent earnouts at fair value of 315,998, equity of 510,561 and deferred payments of 165,164, with goodwill of 1,134,895 and intangible assets of 550,983, and a maximum potential contingent earnout of 544,855 (page:16-19). The purchase accounting is provisional. These businesses contributed total revenues of 202.1 million and a net loss of 42.3 million in six months 2026 (page:17). Management says CAC Group integration is "meaningfully ahead of plan, with approximately 80% of targeted three-year expense synergies already actioned" (Q1 release page:1); that is Management Language and the pack gives no synergy bridge.

Financing and new debt. On 2026-01-02 Amendment No. 4 to the JPM Credit Agreement added 600,000 thousand of incremental term loans on the same terms as the existing Term Loans, with about 12.0 million of debt issuance costs (page:25). No new notes were issued in 2026; the 7.125% Senior Secured Notes due 2031-05-15 remained at 600 million. The company says it intends to fund earnout obligations near term with cash, unused proceeds of the incremental term loans, operating cash flow and revolver borrowings (page:74). The revolver rose from 107,000 thousand to 302,000 thousand over six months 2026, share repurchases were 126,833 thousand, and a 25.0 million deferred payment to a partner was settled on 2026-01-02 (10-K page:189). Use of proceeds therefore combined acquisition funding, earnout and deferred payment settlement and shareholder returns; the pack does not give a sources and uses statement for the add-on, and none is inferred.

Earlier financings, for the timeline: on 2024-05-24 the company issued 600 million of 7.125% Senior Secured Notes and put in place an 840 million first lien term loan and a 600 million revolver (10-K page:161); incremental term loans followed on 2025-01-10 (100.0 million) and 2025-09-18 (75.0 million) (10-K page:164-165).

Disposal. A plan to sell CACH Media Guarantors Insurance Solutions, LLC was committed in Q2 2026 and a definitive agreement for 4.0 million of cash, of which about 2.1 million is in escrow, was signed on 2026-07-02, a subsequent event after the 2026-06-30 balance sheet date (page:46-47). It is immaterial by the company's own assessment.

Share repurchase. On 2026-02-26 the board authorized repurchases of up to 250 million of Class A stock over the following twelve months, with about 124.5 million remaining at 2026-06-30 (page:83; Q4 release page:1).

Creditor read-through. The January 2026 transactions raised debt, equity and non-debt claims together. Leverage mechanics are in the financial base: total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30, against 5.01x at FY2025, with the limit that the earnings include about six months of acquired businesses. The equity component of consideration, 510,561 at fair value, is not a debt claim but dilutes existing holders. Items outside the pack: the Transaction Agreement, the Amendment No. 4 document, the indenture and the credit agreement, so permitted debt, restricted payments and collateral cannot be tested.
### Ownership, control and governance
Documented structure and actions, each with its category.
| Item | Fact | Category | Locator | Mechanic and implication |

| Stockholders agreement history | A putative Class A stockholder sued on 2023-02-08 to invalidate parts of the 2019 Stockholders Agreement. The Court of Chancery held on 2024-05-28 that certain approval rights were facially invalid. The company entered the 2024 Stockholders Agreement on 2024-10-30. On 2026-06-09 the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Court of Chancery and remanded fees; the 2024 Stockholders Agreement "has since sprung into effect replacing in its entirety the 2019 Stockholders Agreement" | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Q2 2026 page:39; 10-K page:182-183 | Insider approval rights are contractually in force again, so board and creditor flexibility on leverage depends on holders |

| Approval rights of holders | While the holders own at least 10% of the shares, the stated approval rights cover a merger or sale of substantially all assets, bankruptcy filing, an acquisition or disposition over 5% of total assets, incurring or refinancing indebtedness over 10% of total assets, equity issuance over 10 million, dividends other than tax distributions, capital expenditure over 5% of total assets, senior management decisions and a change of auditor | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:73, page:75 | A bankruptcy filing, debt incurrence and dividends need holder approval, which affects restructuring flexibility and sponsor-style control without a sponsor |

| Holder consent and independent committee | A consent and defense agreement and an independent committee created in 2024 terminated or were disbanded after the 2026-06-09 ruling | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Q2 2026 page:39-40 | The independent check on the holders' approval rights has been removed |

| How approvals applied to current debt | Whether holders approved the 2025 and 2026 debt additions, and how the 10% of total assets threshold applies to aggregate debt, is not disclosed | Insufficient Information | not stated in the pack | Legal capacity of the issuer to add debt is partly in the holders' hands; the effect cannot be assessed |

| Related-party dealings | Commission revenue from The Villages and affiliates of 2.5 million in FY2025; rent to Villages subsidiaries of about 0.8 million and to other related parties of about 3.1 million; producer commissions to two brothers of the Chairman of about 0.5 million; the Chairman is expected to fund half of a university commitment | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:170-171 | Amounts are small against revenue; no related-party leakage of size is documented |

Governance and sponsor-behaviour read, issuer level only. Supportive: the company states compliance with all indenture and credit agreement covenants at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:162, page:164); disclosure controls were concluded effective at 2026-06-30 (page:82); the auditor's FY2025 report says internal control over financial reporting was maintained effectively in all material respects (10-K page:128). Neutral or mixed: debt-funded acquisitions with equity and earnout components, share repurchases beside revolver draws, and Tax Receivable Agreement payments to insiders. Extraction-oriented or creditor-adverse behaviour is not documented. Legal capacity, what the documents permit: the 10-K gives an incremental facility basket of the greater of 285.0 million and 100% of Consolidated EBITDA plus amounts subject to a 5.50x total first lien net leverage test (10-K page:163); the agreement itself is not supplied. Willingness, what was done: incremental term loans in January 2025, September 2025 and January 2026. ### Conflicts and corrections
Conflicts are logged with both spans and are not reconciled.

| Tax Receivable Agreement liability before 2026 | The 10-K says "we have recorded a Tax Receivable Agreement liability of $4.5 million and $4.8 million, respectively" at 2025-12-31 and 2024-12-31 (page:114) | The Q2 10-Q says "Historically, such amounts were not recorded as we did not expect to realize sufficient cash tax benefits" (page:72) | The liability was small before 2026 under one reading and unrecorded under the other; downstream work should treat the 2026 recognition of 144,570 as new in scale and not state a prior balance of nil |

Corrections to supplied handoffs, stated plainly:

- The source-readiness handoff said legal proceedings are ordinary course with no material adverse effect expected (page:38). That is accurate for the first paragraph only. The same note goes on to describe the stockholder lawsuit and the Delaware Supreme Court ruling of 2026-06-09 (page:39). That handoff should have listed the lawsuit as a governance fact.

- The financial base handoff showed Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities at FY2025 as nil (printed as a dash) and at FY2024 as no line printed. Those refer to the separate balance sheet line. The 10-K also records 4.5 million at 2025-12-31 and 4.8 million at 2024-12-31 inside accrued expenses and other current liabilities (10-K page:177). The 144,570 at 2026-06-30 is correct as printed.

- The financial base handoff said Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities were recognized for the first time as probable in 2026. Read with the conflict above, the accurate statement is that a large liability was first recognized in 2026.
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: commissions follow premium levels and carrier profit-sharing varies, with organic growth of 2% for six months 2026 (10-K page:8; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:60). Mechanic: a soft market lowers premium-based commissions while the people cost base is largely fixed. Implication: margin and debt service capacity are exposed to the premium cycle, and acquired growth does not show underlying durability. The two carriers providing approximately 17% of core commissions and fees counter the diversification across clients.

- Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: the 10-Q shows Tax Receivable Agreement expense of 128.8 million, contingent consideration fair value changes of 14,272 and large addbacks in adjusted EBITDA (financial base). Mechanic: acquisition-related items run through earnings and cash, and earnout payments sit in operating cash flow. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Baldwin has elevated and rising leverage but adequate liquidity and long-dated first-lien debt; the credit view is cautious. Acquired earnings reaching run rate, and covenant headroom, decide the outcome. | Medium | Covenant headroom, pro forma acquired earnings, ratings and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so leverage cannot be tested against its covenant. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt to adjusted EBITDA rose from 4.59x at FY2024 to 5.01x at FY2025 and 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30. | Debt grew faster than reported adjusted earnings, so the cushion against covenant tests and refinancing is thinner. | Medium |

| Adjustments other than interest, amortization and depreciation were 48.6% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA. | Leverage depends on management's earnings definition, and the covenant EBITDA is not supplied. | High |

| Cash was USD 184.5 million and undrawn revolver capacity USD 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against capacity of USD 477.0 million at FY2025. | Liquidity is adequate near term and the revolver is due 2029-05-24, but the buffer has narrowed. | High |

| Pre-IPO holders' approval rights over debt, dividends and a bankruptcy filing are back in force, and there is no sponsor. | Insider-influenced decisions affect leverage tolerance, and how approvals were applied to current debt is not disclosed. | Medium |
### Credit view

Baldwin Insurance Group, Inc. has an elevated-leverage but adequately liquid credit profile, and this synthesis holds that view with Medium confidence. Its strongest support is a diversified, commission-based client base, first-lien debt with no maturity before the revolver on 2029-05-24 beyond scheduled amortization, and USD 184.5 million of cash plus USD 259.4 million of undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-06-30. The weakest point is leverage: total debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 6.30x for the last twelve months to 2026-06-30 from 5.01x at FY2025, on earnings that rely on large addbacks and hold only six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. Whether acquired earnings reach run rate, whether earnout and deferred payments are met without new borrowing, and covenant headroom, which is not supplied, decide the outcome.
### Key findings

First, leverage rose in each period. Baldwin's total debt, including the revolver, was USD 1,435.8 million at FY2024, USD 1,710.6 million at FY2025 and USD 2,495.0 million at 2026-06-30, giving total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.59x, 5.01x and 6.30x, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x [financial base, leverage chart]. The mechanism is the USD 600.0 million incremental term loan of 2026-01-02 and revolver drawings that rose by USD 195.0 million in six months, set against adjusted EBITDA of USD 396.2 million for the last twelve months that includes about six months of the January 2026 acquisitions. The implication is that the 6.30x probably overstates leverage relative to a full-year pro forma basis by an amount the sources do not size, while the use of company-defined earnings could push the other way, so the ratio is an indicator and not a covenant test.

Second, earnings quality limits every ratio. Adjustments other than interest, amortization and depreciation were 42.5% of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and 48.6% of last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, and EBITDA before addbacks, calculated from the statements, was USD 58.1 million for the last twelve months against USD 396.2 million adjusted [financial base]. The gap includes USD 128.8 million of Tax Receivable Agreement expense recognized in six months 2026, which the company adds back although the liability is a future cash obligation. The implication is that creditors who underwrite on adjusted EBITDA are relying on management's definition, and the covenant EBITDA may differ.

Third, interest cover held while leverage rose. Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest was 2.81x at FY2024, 2.96x at FY2025 and 2.89x for the last twelve months, but the six-month figure fell from 3.66x to 3.33x as cash interest rose faster than adjusted earnings [financial base]. About USD 500.0 million of the floating-rate term loans is swapped to a fixed 3.244% to 2028-09-14, and a 100 bp rise in SOFR would add USD 14.0 million a year to interest. The implication is that cover is moderate relative to leverage but protected for part of the rate exposure until 2028.

Fourth, liquidity is adequate and narrowing. Cash and equivalents were USD 184.5 million and company-stated undrawn revolver capacity USD 259.4 million at 2026-06-30, against USD 123.7 million and USD 477.0 million at FY2025, with USD 302.0 million drawn on a USD 600.0 million revolver [financial base, liquidity chart]. Fiduciary cash of USD 426.2 million is excluded because it is fiduciary and not free cash. The mechanism is revolver borrowing used alongside USD 126.8 million of share repurchases and acquisition-related payments in six months 2026. The implication is that near-term liquidity covers scheduled amortization of about USD 16.0 million a year, derived, but it is more exposed to cash calls from earnouts and the Tax Receivable Agreement.

Fifth, claims outside debt are large and time-bound. Contingent earnout liabilities were USD 346.8 million at fair value, with undiscounted expected payments of USD 410.5 million of which USD 131.1 million fall within one year, deferred payments were USD 192.5 million undiscounted, and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities were USD 144.6 million at 2026-06-30 [financial base]. The January 2026 acquisitions cost USD 1,559.6 million in total, of which equity was USD 510.6 million and the maximum potential earnout is USD 544.9 million [business and transaction]. The implication is that the true fixed-claim burden exceeds the debt total, and a strong year for the acquired businesses raises earnout payments in cash.

Sixth, control and governance have changed. The Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Court of Chancery on 2026-06-09, the 2024 Stockholders Agreement is in effect, and holders have stated approval rights over debt above 10% of total assets, dividends, large asset transactions and a bankruptcy filing, while the independent committee created in 2024 has been disbanded [business and transaction]. There is no sponsor, and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented. The implication is that leverage and distribution decisions are insider-influenced, and how approvals were applied to the 2025 and 2026 debt additions is not disclosed, so legal capacity cannot be assessed.

Seventh, the business is diversified by client but not by carrier or cycle. The largest client is under 1% of core commissions and fees, while two insurance partners provided about 17%; commissions follow premium levels, organic revenue growth was 2% for six months 2026 against reported growth of 29%, and the Captive adds underwriting exposure of USD 29.5 million of assumed premium earned in six months 2026 [business and transaction]. The implication is that revenue is durable against any single client but exposed to a soft premium market and carrier appetite, and the growth in the period was bought rather than organic.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Baldwin's client base is highly diversified, with more than three million clients and no client above 1% of core commissions and fees, so single-client loss is not a credit driver [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Its funded debt is long-dated, with the revolver due 2029-05-24 and the term loans and the 7.125% senior secured notes due in 2031, so refinancing risk is back-ended beyond scheduled amortization [financial base; Analyst Interpretation, because the maturity rows are derived]. Liquidity of USD 184.5 million of cash and USD 259.4 million of undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-06-30 covers near-term scheduled amortization many times over [financial base; Documentary Fact for the inputs]. Cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA has stayed near 2.9x across three periods, and part of the floating-rate exposure is fixed by a USD 500.0 million swap at 3.244% to 2028-09-14 [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditures of USD 39.5 million in FY2025, so cash flow is driven by earnouts, interest and acquisitions rather than reinvestment [financial base; Analyst Interpretation]. Management reports faster integration of CAC Group than planned, but this is Management Language and carries no supporting bridge [business and transaction; Management Language].

Weaknesses. Total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.30x for the last twelve months and net debt to adjusted EBITDA 5.83x, up from 5.01x and 4.65x at FY2025, with the denominator holding only about six months of acquired earnings [financial base; Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on addbacks of 48.6% over interest, amortization and depreciation, and the reported result is a net loss of USD 131.8 million for the last twelve months [financial base; Documentary Fact]. All funded debt ranks as first lien and is secured on substantially all assets, so the structure has no subordinated layer beneath the term loans, revolver and notes [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Claims outside debt are material: earnouts of USD 346.8 million, deferred payments of USD 192.5 million and Tax Receivable Agreement liabilities of USD 144.6 million [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Operating cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 43.7 million for the last twelve months and negative USD 68.9 million in FY2025, because earnout payments in excess of the accrual run through operations [financial base; Documentary Fact]. Revenue growth is mostly acquired, with organic growth of 2% for six months 2026 [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Control rests with insiders through approval rights over debt, dividends and a bankruptcy filing, with the independent committee disbanded, and Tax Receivable Agreement payments are owed to LLC members [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. Two insurance partners provided about 17% of core commissions and fees, and the book was historically concentrated in the Southeast [business and transaction; Documentary Fact]. The financial maintenance covenant of 7.00x total first lien net leverage is described only in the FY2025 annual report, with no later reported ratio, so headroom is unmeasured [financial base; Insufficient Information].

| Leverage and refinancing | Debt rose by the USD 600.0 million add-on and revolver drawings while only part of the acquired earnings is in the last-twelve-months figure | Thinner cushion against covenant and market tests; refinancing capacity depends on earnings reaching run rate | Material |

| Claims outside debt | Earnouts, deferred payments and the Tax Receivable Agreement need cash alongside interest and amortization | Cash available for debt service is lower than adjusted free cash flow suggests | Material |

| Insider control | Holders hold approval rights over debt, dividends and a bankruptcy filing; independent committee disbanded | Leverage and distributions are insider-influenced and creditors have limited protection beyond contract; application of approvals is not disclosed | Material |

| Premium cycle and carrier concentration | Commissions follow premiums, two carriers provide about 17% of core commissions and fees, and the book has regional concentrations | A soft market or carrier change reduces revenue and profit-sharing while the people cost base is largely fixed | Material |

| Integration and provisional accounting | Purchase accounting for the 2026 acquisitions is provisional and earnout fair values can change | Earnout and goodwill-related claims may move after the as-of date | Minor |
| Interest rate | Floating term loans and revolver, with USD 500.0 million swapped to 3.244% to 2028-09-14 | A 100 bp rise adds USD 14.0 million a year to interest | Minor |
## Calculations

No new calculation is made in this module. Every figure is taken from the supplied financial base or the business and transaction handoff and is restated in USD millions rounded to one decimal from the thousand-dollar figures, for example 1,435,800 thousand as USD 1,435.8 million. Directional statements rest on the paired figures cited: total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.59x, 5.01x and 6.30x; net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 4.31x, 4.65x and 5.83x; adjusted EBITDA to cash interest of 2.81x, 2.96x and 2.89x, and 3.66x falling to 3.33x between six months 2025 and six months 2026. The statement that the last-twelve-months ratio is probably higher than a full-year pro forma ratio is an interpretation of the stated acquisition dates, not a calculation, and is marked as such.
